einstellungen.text: Your mom is walking alone through a dark forest right now. And you're going out to meet her.
“I'm staying right behind you. If I scream, it's not a joke.”
Out here, there are new rules. Don't answer. Don't split up. Don't stop.
The beam is shaking because your hand is shaking. Ben is holding on to your backpack.
It's one in the morning. The ground is wet. Every time a branch snaps, your heart stops for a second.
Somewhere up in the trees: click. Click. It's following you.
Then Mom calls. From the left.
“Honey! I'm over here!”
And then Mom calls again. From the right.
“Honey, not that way! Over here!”
“Which one? Which one is it?”
Two voices. Both sound exactly like her. One of them is not your mother.
You take a deep breath. And you shout the one word only the two of you know.
“Lighthouse!”
From the left, the voice answers right away. “Lighthouse! Lighthouse!” It just repeats your word.
From the right, there's no answer. Instead, a small light blinks. Three times. Like a lighthouse.
That's the sign. A voice can be copied. A light can't.
You run. Mom is standing in the fog with her phone light. Her jacket smells like rain and gasoline.
“I'm here. I'm right here.”
You hold her so tight she laughs. And you laugh too, even though you're crying.
On the way back, nobody talks. Mom holds your hand. Like back when you were little.
Just before two, the three of you sit by the fireplace. The door is locked twice.
Ben sits very still next to you. He doesn't even touch the last slice of toast.
“From now on, we go grocery shopping together. All of us.”
“Remember? You used to yell Lighthouse every night. Just so I'd come back in.”
“Yeah. Every night.”
You realize how long it's been since you hugged her this tight. Years, maybe.
Then someone calls from outside. In Ben's voice. “Hey! Open up! I'm still out here!”
You look next to you. Ben is sitting on the couch. He hasn't said a word since you got back.
Grandpa's watch on his wrist has stopped ticking.
